chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked him about the junub who enters janabah and then wants to sleep. He said: “If he wishes to perform wudu (ablution), then let him do so, and ghusl is better than that. And if he sleeps without performing wudu (ablution) and without performing ghusl, then there is nothing upon him, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more virtuous or superior in merit
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: any liability, blame, or required consequence
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required after janabah

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah sleep before performing ghusl or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one in the state of janabah who wishes to sleep before performing ghusl. It indicates that wudu (ablution) before sleep is permissible and recommended, ghusl is more virtuous, and sleeping without either does not incur liability.
